label: input y early in the original sequence (positions 0-2)
explanation: Token-and-position feature: fires only when the input token is y during the original phase at steps 0-2 (about 26% of all y inputs, and essentially every early y). Magnitude falls off with position: mean about 1.68 at t=0, 1.39 at t=1, 0.74 at t=2, and weak sparse firing (about 0.15) at t=3 on roughly 10% of y-at-t=3 steps. The strongest examples are y at t=1 after t. It is silent for y at t>=4, for every other token, at the delimiter, and in the copy phase (including when y is being output). Repeated early y (in_first=0) still fires, but more weakly.

issues: Minor systematic false-positive pocket: y at t=2 when orig(0)=='l' (e.g. 'l 1 y', 'l a y') is inactive about 14% of the time (precision 0.86 on 519 test steps). It accounts for most of the 73 test false positives. It is too small to change the verdict, and excluding it lowers F1 (0.979).

Misses are all y at t=3 with weak activation (0.01-0.27 relative), holding 0.4% of the mass. This matches the explanation's t=3 caveat. Adding t=3 drops test precision to 0.776 (F1 0.874), so leaving it out is justified.

Profile confirms the rest: all activation mass is on in_tok=y; the delimiter never fires; the copy phase fires once in 2.7M steps; mass share falls by position (t0 0.44, t1 0.37, t2 0.19), consistent with the claimed falling magnitude; y at t=3 is active on about 10% of steps. Test precision 0.9985, recall 0.968, F1 0.983 reproduced.
A repeated early y (in_first==0) fires with precision 1.0, consistent with the claim that it still fires (more weakly).
